Nourishing face moisturiser for dry, sensitive skin

The face
Published in full, every ingredient and every percentage

Flow is our face texture. It carries a little over ten percent plant oils, which is generous for something this light, and it is built around the oils that suit dry skin with a low irritation threshold: avocado for cushioning richness, safflower and evening primrose for barrier lipids, baobab and jojoba for softness that does not feel occlusive.

Around those sits the same supporting cast that runs through every Biotaderm formula. A postbiotic ferment, a prebiotic, plant squalane, allantoin, vitamin E. The formula is built at skin pH, held there by sodium citrate, which is the plainest thing we do for the skin microbiome and the best evidenced.

It suits skin that is dry, tight after washing, and quick to complain about new products.

Warm a small amount between your fingertips and press it into clean skin, once or twice a day, before any cosmetics or sunscreen. Only a little is needed. If your skin is highly reactive, patch test first.

Five oils do the work here, chosen for dry, sensitive skin rather than for how they read on a label. Each has its own entry in the ingredient library, with the evidence and its limits set out in full.

Avocado Oil Persea Gratissima

The richest oil in this formula and the most abundant. High in oleic acid, it cushions and softens, which is what dry skin tends to want most. Ours is organic, cold-pressed and upcycled from fruit that would otherwise be waste.

Safflower Seed Oil Carthamus Tinctorius

A high-linoleic oil, and linoleic acid is one of the fatty acids the skin barrier is actually built from. The research on linoleic-rich plant oils in barrier repair is among the better developed in this area, which is why this one is here in quantity rather than as a gesture.

Evening Primrose Oil Oenothera Biennis

One of the few plant oils rich in gamma-linolenic acid. Studies suggest GLA-rich oils support barrier function in skin that is dry and easily provoked, and it has a long record of comfortable use on reactive skin.

Baobab Seed Oil Adansonia Digitata

A balanced oil that softens and helps skin hold onto moisture, without the heaviness of the more occlusive butters. Organic and cold-pressed.

Jojoba Seed Oil Simmondsia Chinensis

Technically a liquid wax rather than an oil, and close enough in structure to the skin's own sebum that it sits well on most people. It conditions without feeling like a layer.

Bladderwrack Fucus Vesiculosus, our signature Atlantic seaweed

The same species you will find on the rocks below Welcombe at low tide. Ours is a cold, solvent-free infusion in sunflower oil, made in the UK, and we would rather be plain about what that form carries. The fucoidans and phlorotannins the seaweed is famous for are water-soluble and largely stay behind. What crosses into the oil is fucoxanthin, the golden pigment, which gives a modest antioxidant note. That, and a real kinship with the coast this brand comes from, is why it is here. It is in every formula we make.

Beyond these, every Biotaderm moisturiser shares the same quiet supporting cast: squalane, a postbiotic ferment upcycled from gin distilling, prebiotic inulin, allantoin, vitamin E and chlorella.
About the vetiver, and why this is not fragrance-free

There is one essential oil in this formula. Vetiver root oil, at a tenth of a percent, chosen for the antioxidant properties the research credits it with and for the quiet earthy note it gives the blend. It is named on the label under its own name, never folded into a "parfum" catch-all.

That means the honest description of this product is "no synthetic fragrance" rather than "fragrance-free". One is true. The other would not be. A concentrated aromatic can still be a lot for a fragile barrier, which is why the level is kept low and why a patch test is worth the trouble if your skin runs reactive.
